options.metric: Share of crashes with at least one person injured or killed
options.denominator: All police-reported crashes in the time period
options.reason: A casualty-involved crash share directly compares how often a reported crash has a human harm outcome across night and day crashes.
options.answer: These records cannot establish whether NYC streets are more dangerous per trip at night, but 28.5% of reported night crashes involved an injury or death, compared with 23.5% of day crashes.
options.interpretation: This framing answers whether a reported crash was more likely to involve a casualty at night, and the chart shows a higher share at night. Comparing casualty crashes with all crashes is a defensible crash-severity measure, but it leaves unanswered the risk per trip or mile because traffic and road-user exposure are not in the data.

options.metric: Share of crashes with at least one person killed
options.denominator: All police-reported crashes in the time period
options.reason: Fatal crashes provide a focused comparison of the most severe recorded crash outcome.
options.answer: The data cannot determine per-trip nighttime danger, but fatal crashes made up 0.290% of night crashes versus 0.108% of daytime crashes.
options.interpretation: This framing answers whether a reported crash was more likely to be fatal at night, and the chart shows a larger fatal-crash share at night. Fatality is a clear severe outcome and the denominator is all reported crashes in each period, but the comparison does not measure risk per trip or mile without exposure data.

options.metric: Average number of police-reported crashes per clock hour per observed date
options.denominator: 5,094 dates with crash records, for each clock hour
options.reason: Hourly crash counts show when crashes occur most often while avoiding unequal totals from day and night covering different numbers of hours.
options.answer: These records cannot establish per-road-user risk, but reported crashes averaged 5.4 per date at 3am and peaked at 31.7 per date at 4pm.
options.interpretation: This framing answers how reported crash volume varies across the clock, with the chart showing lower counts in most overnight hours and a late-afternoon peak. Counts per clock hour per observed date make hourly volumes comparable, but without traffic or road-user exposure they cannot establish whether an individual is more likely to crash at night.
